paper.title: Dynamic recrystallization behavior and microstructure evolution of low-density high-strength Fe-Mn-Al-C steel
paper.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
paper.paper_scope: Hot deformation behavior and dynamic recrystallization of a single low-density high-strength Fe-25.14Mn-10Al-1.46C-0.053Nb steel were studied by isothermal constant-strain-rate compression at 900-1150 °C and 0.01-10 s^-1; the work derives DRX characteristic-value (critical/peak/steady-state) models, a DRX state diagram, and a DRX average grain size prediction model.

alloys.description: Single heat (forging billet) of low-density high-strength Fe-Mn-Al-C steel; used to study hot deformation and dynamic recrystallization behavior via isothermal compression tests.
alloys.alloys_notes: Composition reported as mass fraction (%); Fe is the balance. Same steel batch/composition used to confirm reproducibility under identical experimental conditions.

unmapped_findings: Dynamic recrystallization activation energy Qp = 669.844 kJ/mol, computed via the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine equation with average slopes k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690; reported as an average value within the experimental range (b0032, b0085).
Zener-Hollomon parameter lnZ values for all 24 T/ε̇ conditions are tabulated: lnZ rises as ε̇ increases or T decreases (b0037, b0041).

Models relating DRX characteristic values to lnZ were established: εc = 0.0093 lnZ - 0.43, εp = 0.020 lnZ - 0.94, εs = 0.034 lnZ - 1.53 and quadratic σc, σp, σs expressions; εc/εp ≈ 0.452 (b0054, b0057).
A dynamic recrystallization state diagram was drawn with area A (work hardening), area B (partial DRX) and area C (complete DRX) (b0058).

DRX average grain size prediction model: d_rex = 807743.63 ε̇^-0.1903 exp(-120648.47/RT) + 4.338; model correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%, with absolute error generally below 3 μm (b0075, b0080).
Recommended hot working window for fine and uniform DRX grains: 950-1000 °C/0.01-0.1 s^-1 and 1050-1100 °C/1-10 s^-1 (b0065, b0086).

Three deformation zones were characterized in the compressed samples: 1 - difficult deformation zone, 2 - small deformation zone, 3 - large deformation zone; DRX degree order zone 3 > zone 2 > zone 1 (b0060, b0066).

Initial microstructure of the forged billet was observed before deformation (Fig. 1), and microstructures were imaged with a LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope using a 30% nitric acid alcohol etchant (b0018, b0022).

The steel is reported as a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material; reproducibility of the experimental phenomena was explicitly checked on the same composition batch (b0018, b0024).

Finite element simulation of the compression was performed with DEFORM-3D, shear friction 0.3 and billet-air convection coefficient 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C), to build the grain-size prediction model input (b0068, b0070).
